claim: A high nugget-to-sill ratio suggests weak spatial dependence or strong short-range/noise effects, so kriging-based maps require cautious interpretation.
conditions: Applies when nugget and sill are estimated from a meaningful experimental variogram with enough point pairs.
limitations: High nugget can reflect measurement error, microscale variability, sampling support mismatch, or true weak spatial autocorrelation.
recommended_action: Flag high nugget/sill, inspect outliers and sampling density, and avoid high confidence in local map details.
not_allowed_action: Do not assign a high final grade when nugget/sill is very high and validation is weak.
